IS: 12461 ( Part 2)- 1988 



Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2005 ) 

SIMPLIFIED PRESENTATION OF TECHNICAL DOCUMENTS 

PART 2 GUIDE FOR PREPARATION OF ORDER DRAWINGS 
FOR BOUGHT-OUT PARTS 



1. Scope — Lays down the guidelines for the preparation of order drawings for non-standardized 
bought-out parts which are generally covered by catalogues and prospectus and of the manu- 
facturer, without violating the copyright act. This will ensure uniform quality and freedom from the 
risk of changes effected by the manufacturer in his own document. 

2. Guide for the Preparation of Order Drawings 

2.1 The order drawings for bought-out items shall be clear for manufacture inspection and also 
for ordering. 

2.2 if circumstances permit, the figures from the catalogue may be copied out and pasted on to a 
preprinted format and the details not covered in the catalogue but essential, shall be incorporated 
in the format in the form of notes as illustrated in Fig. 1. 

2.3 The order drawings for bought-out parts are meant for purchase of item and cannot be used 
for manufacture, since the drawing contains only essential dimensions. Further, it should be made 
clear by indicating on the drawing 'BOUGHT-OUT PART' above the title block at the right hand 
side together with details regarding the supplier (see Fig. 2 and 3 ). 

3. Obligations — The technical particulars and quality requirements of the order given by the 
purchaser on bought-out parts drawings have to be adhered to by the supplier, even in case of any 
revision in the document ( catalogue, prospectus, etc ) of the manufacturer.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard is one of the series of standards on simplified presentation of technical docu- 
ments. Other standards are as follows: 

IS ; 10967-1984 Guide for presentation of variant drawings 

IS ; 10968-1984 Drawing practice for simplified presentation 

IS : 12461 ( Part 1 )-1988 Simplified presentation of technical documents. 

Part 1 Guide for presentation of supplementary drawings 

In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from DIN 30 Part 5-1976 'Simplified 
representation in technical documents, foreign-part drawings ( order drawings ) directions for 
preparing', issued by the Deutsches institute fur Normung, Germany. 

Order drawings are prepared for the purpose of documentation of non-standardized commer- 
cial components which in general are covered in prospectus and catalogues. With the availability 
of order drawings, one need not depend on the original documents of the supplier which over a 
period of time may get altered and during later delivery, the document cannot be located easily 
when they are substituted by new issue. 

Order-drawings can be prepared without actually executing the drawing-work. Figures and 
tables or descriptive texts can be copied from the document available on hand (advertising 
material and prospectus, catalogue, etc ) then cut and pasted on to a preprinted drawing format. 

Each organization can apply order-drawing for more or less with the following obvious 
advantages. 

a) Clear stipulation of non-standardized components. The insufficient data/clarity of repre- 
sentation in the catalogue/prospectus can be suitably supplemented in order drawings. 

b) Deliveries are independent of suppliers documents. 

c) Uniform documents for numbering of the components and repeated parts. 

d) For purchase activity, a distinct document and for ordering, only a short text wherein only 
the title and the number of the drawing could be indicated. 

The manufacturer of the commercial products should as far as possible plan the drawing of 
the product in their catalogues in such a way that the users can take out the data directly from the 
catalogue and add the other data pertaining to their organization. 



Printed at New India Printing Press, Khuria, Ind'a
